title: Automated 'Forget Me' Deletion Workflow and Verifiable Evidence Harness
creator: Priya Nair
description: Build an end-to-end automated Right-To-Be-Forgotten (RTBF) orchestration that covers hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. The feature must: 1) allow customers to configure retention policies and one-off deletion requests by residency zone; 2) execute deletions across storage tiers (object stores, databases, caches, and backups) with idempotency guarantees; 3) produce tamper-evident, verifiable evidence artifacts for each deletion action that customers and auditors can consume; 4) expose a verification API and console reporting for compliance teams; and 5) integrate with existing audit logs, KMS/HSM signing, and retention enforcement schedulers.
acceptance_criteria: Customers can submit an RTBF request via API and Console with residency and scope selection.
Deletion orchestration runs to completion or fails with clear retryable/exception status and emits a single canonical deletion event per resource.

For each RTBF action, a signed deletion receipt (JSON) is generated containing: resource identifiers (hashed where required), timestamp, execution steps, operator IDs (system component), provenance hashes, and a KMS-backed signature.
Verification API accepts a deletion receipt and returns a cryptographic verification result and a human-readable audit summary.
Retention enforcement scheduler enforces retention windows (policy-level) and generates deletion jobs that appear in the console and are traceable in logs and dashboards.
Support can run cross-region diagnostics and replay runs for customer-facing audits without exposing raw PII in logs; all exported evidence uses salted hashes.
Automated tests cover happy path, multi-shard deletion, interrupted job recovery, and deletion proof validation with simulated KMS keys.
Rollout can be toggled per-organization and supports canary on Dedicated/Private deployments with feature flags.

comments: 2026-02-22 Priya Nair: Kickoff meeting notes - scoped to supported resource types (objects, embeddings, request logs, KV cache entries, and derived indexes). Decided to exclude immutable legal holds for first cut.

2026-02-28 Javier Ortega: Proposed state machine attached in design doc. Chosen approach: persistent job record + step-level compensating actions. Trade-off: longer implementation time vs. stronger auditability.
2026-03-03 Emma Chen (Security): Requested KMS integration and HSM-backed signing for receipts. Also requested a redact-first logging policy and retention mask for evidence exports.
2026-03-06 Michael Park (SRE): Suggested adding cross-region verification checks to detect partial deletions caused by network partitioning; will prototype in staging.
2026-03-09 PM Review: Updated acceptance criteria to require salted hashes for exported resource identifiers and a verification API schema. Created tickets for console UX edge cases.
metrics_and_alerts: Metric: deletion_job.mean_time_to_complete (SLO: 95% within 5m for small jobs)
Alert: any receipt-signing failure triggers high-priority security alert
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable for internal org and 3 pilot customers on Hosted API.
Phase 2: open for Dedicated customers with opt-in flag and enable per-region controls.
Phase 3: private deployments - provide migration guide and operator commands for signing key rotation.
Fallback: automatic halt and rollback to 'mark-failed' state if >5% jobs enter permanent failed state during canary.
notes: Design decision: receipts will include salted hashed identifiers rather than raw PII to minimize exposure while preserving verifiability.
Constraint: some backup/archival systems are append-only; we'll provide a documented exception path involving legal holds and a certified purge timeline rather than immediate deletion.
Open question: whether to expose whole-replayable proof bundles for third-party auditors or deliver verified summaries only. Security recommends summary-first with auditor escrow flow.
audit_proof_format: Canonical JSON receipt: {version, receipt_id, hashed_resources[], residency_zone, steps[{action, target, outcome, timestamp}], signature(kms_key_id)}, persisted in immutable audit bucket and indexable via job id.
legal_requirements: GDPR: Article 17 requirements for erasure and proof of compliance
CCPA: consumer deletion and record-keeping obligations
Schrems II considerations for cross-border transfers; per-region residency enforcement required
implementation_constraints: Private deployments may not allow outbound KMS signing; provide local-signing adapter pattern and document operator steps.
Backups and long-term archives: coordinate with storage infra team to mark objects for purge with retention windows instead of synchronous deletion where necessary.
Need to avoid synchronous bulk deletes in hot request path to preserve latency SLOs.
